subject: IaC policy lint + network egress encapsulation for on-prem stack - review
messages:
From: Acme Financial <infra@acme-fin.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: DC Ops <datacenter-ops@dcops.com>
Date: 2028-06-20T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: evidence & checklist for on-prem egress encapsulation + IaC lint

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our security team wants a concise checklist and any module-level diffs showing our required egress encapsulation (NAT + proxy hop + metadata egress allow list) applied to Redwood's private stack. They also asked that the Terraform/Helm/Ansible bundles pass a policy lint step (we run OPA/Gatekeeper) and that CI gating prevents merges that weaken egress rules.

Can you provide: 1) a short checklist we can use for the SOC proof pack, 2) any planned module changes (Terraform) that will add the encapsulation, and 3) the CI change you propose so their devops pipeline can validate before we sync to prod?

We are targeting a non-disruptive rollout — canary to staging first.

Attachments: none from us yet.

Best,
Clara Reyes
Infra Security Lead, Acme Financial
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Clara Reyes <infra@acme-fin.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, datacenter-ops@dcops.com
Date: 2028-06-20T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: evidence & checklist for on-prem egress encapsulation + IaC lint

Clara — thanks, this is clear.

Quick plan:
- Attached: iac-policy-checklist.pdf (SOC-style checklist) and a small tf patch (tf-module-diff.patch) showing the encapsulation changes scoped to the private-network module.
- CI gating proposal: a new pipeline stage in gitlab-ci (policy-lint + staged-apply simulation using terraform plan + helm template + ansible --check). If policy-lint or plan simulation fails, MR cannot be merged to main.
- Non-disruptive rollout: feature flag in module (encapsulation.enabled=false by default), staged rollout to staging via canary tag, then flip in prod after validation.

Action items for Redwood internal: can Hannah and Irene validate the tf/helm diffs and confirm there are no hidden secret exposures or service account scope enlargements? Vivek — can you sign off on the CI step and the suggested runner sizing for plan-sim tests?

I'll drop the artifacts in the Drive link and we can iterate.

Jonas
VP, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
Attachments: iac-policy-checklist.pdf, tf-module-diff.patch
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-20T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: evidence & checklist for on-prem egress encapsulation + IaC lint

Thanks — I reviewed tf-module-diff.patch at a high level. Notes:
- Terraform: private-network/module/main.tf -> added aws_nat_gateway + proxy hop routing table entries and a new variable encapsulation.metadata_allowlist. The change is scoped to interface attachments and does not touch instance profiles.
- Helm: suggested values additions include envoy sidecar.enabled + egress.proxy.cluster config. Helm templates in chart/common/egress.yaml will need conditional templating when sidecar is off for older stacks.
- Ansible: playbook network/validate_egress.yml includes verification steps (tcp connect to proxy hop, metadata endpoint deny-by-default). We added ansible --check tests to pipeline.

Concerns:
1) Terraform module uses count on nat gateway resource keyed by az; need to ensure drift handling is robust in partial AZ replacement — add lifecycle.ignore_changes for allocation_id on gateway if we expect manual replacements.
2) Helm conditional must not create duplicate ServiceMonitor resources in clusters where monitoring is managed externally. I'll add a guard to avoid conflicts.

I'll open two small PR branches for tf and helm fixes and reference this thread.

- Hannah

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>

Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-20T14:18:00-07:00
Subject: Quick question on default proxy ACLs

DC Ops — two quick operational questions before we finalize the checklist:
1) What are the default outbound ACL timeouts on the proxy appliances? We need to align terraform healthcheck timeout and ansible validation windows.
2) For maintenance windows that require temporary relaxed egress (for updates), what is your recommended short-lived exception pattern so we can code an automated toggle in the Ansible runbook?

On receipt: DC Ops replied inline: 
- \"Default outbound ACL timeout is 30s; for heavy loads we can bump to 60s but it'll be billed as connection-time.
- Recommended pattern: admission control tag 'egress-temp-allow' with a TTL and an audit log entry. Use vault-wrapped token for the toggle and ensure the toggle playbook records the change in evidence_manifest.csv.\"

Irene
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Clara Reyes <infra@acme-fin.com>, irene_choi@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, datacenter-ops@dcops.com

Clara — does that timeline work for you? If so we'll assign the Drive link and kick off the PRs this week.

Thanks all — will follow up once PRs land.

Jonas

Redwood Inference
